chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) did not see any problem with blood that was not slaughtered, if it happens to be in the garment, so the man prays in it – meaning the blood of the fish.
ai.seo_question: Is fish blood considered pure for prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that fish blood is considered pure (tahir) and does not invalidate prayer, distinguishing it from the blood of land animals which requires ritual slaughter (dhabihah). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the blood of creatures not requiring specific slaughter, such as fish, is inherently clean, reflecting the broader principle of purity in aquatic life.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that
Aliasws did not see any problem with blood what does not get slaughtered, if it happens to be in the clothes, so the man prays Salaat in it – meaning the blood of the fish’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
‘Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would not consider the blood of things that did not require slaughtering as harmful to one’s Salah (prayer). That is, the blood of fish.’”
